native_mechanisms: The die-stone never resets between marks: one running state carries the callus of every prior fold.

Each mark's weight is pressed into the stone's already-turned position, so early marks bend how later marks land (order-dependent, path-dependent, differences amplified so differing paths never re-merge).
Only the stone's final seated reading against the fixed keeps leaves the desk; all intermediate turns and residue are swept away.
core_technique: xxHash64-style construction: 8-byte little-endian loads folded into never-reset 64-bit accumulators via rotate(add)-multiply rounds — four interleaved lanes over 64-byte stripes for len>=64 (single accumulator with an extra per-word multiply for short inputs), then lane merge plus a standard xor-shift/multiply avalanche finalizer — i.e. the known multiply-xor-shift accumulator approach plus generic ILP striping, not a mechanism derived from the native's imagery.
